facts.statement: The genus Lutungutali was named in 2013 based on a single holotype fossil specimen containing hip bones and tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Lutungutali was named in 2013 and described from a fossil specimen, holotype NHCC LB32, including hip bones and tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Lutungutali were collected in 2009 from the upper Ntawere Formation, dating to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected in 2009 from the upper Ntawere Formation, which dates to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.

facts.statement: The known fossil remains of Lutungutali consist of parts of the pelvis and four caudal vertebrae forming the base of the tail.
facts.quote: Lutungutali is known from parts of its pelvis and from four caudal vertebrae that make up the base of the tail.

facts.statement: Lutungutali belongs to the family Silesauridae, a group of archosaurs very closely related to Dinosauria.
facts.quote: Lutungutali belongs to Silesauridae, a family of archosaurs that is very closely related to Dinosauria.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the presence of derived avemetatarsalians like Lutungutali in the Middle Triassic indicates a rapid diversification of this group earlier than previously thought.
facts.quote: Because Asilisaurus and Lutungutali are relatively derived members of Avemetatarsalia, their presence in the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic suggests that avemetatarsalians underwent a rapid diversification at a time in their evolutionary history that was earlier than previously thought.

facts.statement: Lutungutali is classified within the unranked order Ornithodira.
Lutungutali is classified in the family Silesauridae.
The genus Lutungutali was established by Peecook et al. in 2013.
The type species of the genus Lutungutali is Lutungutali sitwensis.
Silesaurids, the family to which Lutungutali belongs, have been found in southern Africa, Poland, the southwestern United States, and South America.
facts.quote: Los silesáuridos se han encontrado en África meridional, Polonia, el suroeste de Estados Unidos y Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The closest silesaurid to Lutungutali is Asilisaurus from the Anisian-age Manda Formation of Tanzania.
facts.quote: El silesáurido más cercano a Lutungutali es Asilisaurus, de la época del Anisiense de Tanzania, ambos encontrados en la formación Manda.

facts.statement: Before the discovery of Asilisaurus, the oldest known avemetatarsalians were from the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, antes del descubrimiento de Asilisaurus (que fue nombrado en 2010), los avemetatarsalianos más antiguos conocidos eran de la etapa Ladiniense del Triásico Medio.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Sulcimentisauria as the parent group for Lutungutali.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Lutungutali within the class Ornithischia.
